hook.text: Shouting in a quiet library is easy to hear. Whispering at a rock concert is impossible. That's SNR in action.

buildup.text: Signal-to-noise ratio measures how much stronger the signal is compared to the background noise.

discovery.text: SNR is measured in decibels. Every 10 dB increase means the signal is ten times stronger relative to noise.

twist.text: High SNR doesn't mean no noise. It means the signal dominates enough that noise becomes ignorable.

climax.text: Shannon's channel capacity formula directly depends on SNR. Higher SNR means more bits per second.

punchline.text: Louder signal, quieter noise, better communication.

quiz.question: What does a higher signal-to-noise ratio indicate?
options: The signal is much stronger than the noise
